sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the path segment of the matching endpoint. getUserByEmail checks the address against a deliberately loose shape rule, one @ with non-empty whitespace-free parts, and refuses anything else before dispatch; its comment records that single-label domains and domain literals are legitimate on self-hosted, LDAP, AD and SSO instances and that authoritative format validation is TestRail's. getUsers takes an optional project and addresses get_users/{project_id} when it is given. updateGroup injects the path identifier into the body as group_id, overwriting whatever the caller supplied, because TestRail rejects a body without it. No write payload is parsed by a public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

UserSchema is the reply shape and is permissive: role_id, is_admin, group_ids and the enterprise fields are all nullish because older servers omit them and get_current_user returns a reduced record, and mfa_required admits an integer because TestRail Cloud wire-encodes it as 0 or 1. UserAddPayloadSchema requires a non-empty name and an email in a dotted-domain format, and declares role_id, group_ids and assigned_projects as positive integers; UserUpdatePayloadSchema makes every field optional. GroupSchema carries id, name and a nullish user_ids. AddGroupPayloadSchema requires name; UpdateGroupPayloadSchema makes it optional and its comment records that TestRail accepts an empty update body. RoleSchema carries id, name, is_default and a nullish is_project_admin.

get_group and get_groups return a group and an envelope of groups. add_group takes name and user_ids; update_group supports the same fields and states that a supplied user_ids sets the group's members to match it exactly, with no way to add or remove one member. delete_group returns no group data.

input_policy.notes: One identifier in the path and no request body, so every field beyond it is refused.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the group and the IDs of its members; user_ids is nullish in the driver's reply schema, so an absent membership is not an error. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.

parameters.semantics: The group to read. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.
